statistic_definition: D_fresh = N(E,R) - N(B,R), N(X,R) = A(X,R)/sqrt(A(X,X)*A(R,R)); A pooled share of same-problem pairs of finished wrong answers (v3 wrong, no cap hit, extracted answer present) that agree under math-verify 0.9.0 (rln4_lib.agree on norm_v3, pair in sorted order)

adversary.how: D_alt = N(S,R) - N(B,R) with Think-SFT + cue (sft1_cue_s4-01) as S, on fresh2026 problems where S, R, B and the edit each have >= 1 finished wrong answer; within pairs from problems where the model has >= 2; bootstrap 10,000 problem resamples, default_rng(16)

null_base_23_vs_01.how: X = base samples 2-3, B = base samples 0-1, each against R, on the statistic's rows where both halves have >= 1 finished wrong answer

rule: verdict16: holds if the 90 % interval is inside the range, n >= 50 and the interval excludes the adversary's value; inside but containing it: not separated; wholly outside: refuted; else undecided
departures: The edit's rows are not in git: read from the four one-sample runs named in mixvote/fresh2026_top8x1.5-01/run.json (runs/ih-1115-*, answers.jsonl); sample index taken from the seed.
Agreement uses the team grader's math-verify equivalence (rln4_lib.agree on norm_v3), with each pair in sorted order so cross pairs do not depend on the argument order.

The adversary's rows (S, R, B and E each >= 1 finished wrong answer) give n = 32, not >= 50: Think-SFT has 176 cap hits on these problems, so few finished wrong answers; without the edit condition n = 34 and D_alt = 0.0112.
Bootstrap draws in which X or B has zero agreeing within pairs give no N and are dropped and counted (adversary: 2 of 10,000; statistic: 0; null: 548).
The null's rows are the statistic's rows where both base halves have >= 1 finished wrong answer (n 37).
raw_rows_note: Read the 10 rows above plus the edit's full texts for problems 2 and 5: every row is an integer AIME-style answer taken from a final \boxed{}, finish_reason stop, no cap hit, no loop flag; extraction matches the box in each text. Repeated wrong values are real (the edit gives 145 three times on problem 5, gold 396; RL gives 65 twice on problem 2, gold 70), so agreement measures shared wrong values, not extraction artifacts. Seeds: within a model each (problem, sample) seed is distinct; across models the same seed rule (7000000 + 10000*sample + index) is used by design, and E and B share prompt and seed (both cued), while R has no prefix, so a shared random stream cannot inflate E-R or B-R pairs more than E-B. Cap hits on the 69 rows (of 276 slots per model): edit 28, RL 46, base 120, Think-SFT 176; the base's and Think-SFT's finished wrong answers are a minority of their samples, so their within-pair shares rest on few pairs (base 118 pairs, Think-SFT 36). Some edit answers finish near the cap (14,266 and 14,432 of 16,384 tokens).
